chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Burayd, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the slave (mamluk), is his testimony valid? He said, 'Yes, and indeed the first person to reject the testimony of the slave was so-and-so.'

key_terms.اَلْمَمْلُوكِ: The slave or servant, a specific legal status in classical fiqh
key_terms.لَفُلاَنٌ: It was so-and-so (referring to a specific person)

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a slave (mamluk) valid in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirms the legal validity of a *mamluk*'s testimony, challenging the prevailing view that their status as property disqualified them from bearing witness. By identifying the first person to reject their testimony, the Imam highlights a specific historical deviation in jurisprudential practice, reinforcing the Shia principle that legal capacity is not strictly bound by social hierarchy but by justice and reliability.
